turns.reply:
The screen layer rework is pushed and open as [fischerq/ludumdare60#59](https://github.com/fischerq/ludumdare60/pull/59). It loads with no console errors, and the playtest bot finishes the layer every time. I tested it in a phone-size browser window, not on a real phone.

**What changed in the screen layer:**
- **Speeds:** the beam takes 13 s per picture instead of 10. Pac-Man walks 6.5 tiles/s there instead of 5.
- **Enemies:** the red ghosts are gone, so the beam is the only danger. There are no regular dots to collect any more.
- **Goals:** four pads on the edge of the tube, one for each adjustment of a real monitor. Until you set one, the beam paints that fault into the picture:
  - **V-HOLD** (left): the picture rolls.
  - **H-HOLD** (bottom): the rows tear sideways.
  - **CONVERGE** (top, under the gun): red and blue fringes.
  - **DEGAUSS** (right): blotches of wrong colour.

  Walk onto a pad and the beam paints that part right from then on. Since the beam only hurts where it paints light, each fix also moves where you can get hit. The line under the counter lists what's left and says what each fix did.
- **Bonus dots:** the four power pellets, eaten while they glow. The first one makes the beam scan column by column for 15 s, the next one bottom to top.
- **Feedback:** Pac-Man lights up and briefly grows on every pickup. The glowing Pac-Man is new art in `assets/deep/crt/pac-glow-0..3` for Max to redraw.

I picked the four adjustments myself. They're marked proposed in `design/systems/layer-deep.md`, so swap them if you had something else in mind.

**Other layers where the goal doesn't match what the part does** (written into the same doc as open):
- **Video RAM:** disconnected. You eat pellet bytes, which doesn't show that it holds the picture.
- **Bus:** half. You pick up a byte, but it never reaches the CPU.
- **CPU:** half. Reaching a routine has no visible effect.
- **Game logic:** half. Standing on a ghost's target tile does nothing.
- **Dots:** in layers -3 to -7 they're only counted.
- **Video board and input wires:** these two fit already.

**One concern:** a perfect player clears the layer in about 10 s. The bot took about 70 s when playing badly, but 1 to 3 minutes per run probably needs more goals or harder ones. The playtest results file still has the old numbers for this layer, since a full rerun is slow.

**Test on the phone:** go to layer -1 and walk to each pad. The picture should stop rolling, stop tearing, lose its fringes and lose its blotches, one by one. Eat a glowing pellet and check that the beam switches to columns, then bottom to top, and that Pac-Man glows.

Usage was 2% of the 5-hour window and 23% of the week at the start of this turn.
